title: Deployment Surge After-Action + Canary Tactics
summary: After-action notes for the Jan 22 deployment surge that triggered canary errors and a rapid hotfix. Root causes appear tied to a batching optimization change + KV cache TTL mismatch; autoscaler edge-case prevented timely scale-up in us-west1. Document captures timeline, mitigations, revised canary acceptance criteria, and action items.
content:
Meeting: Deployment Surge After-Action + Canary Tactics
Date: 2025-01-22 (notes taken during review meeting)
Owners: Aisha Patel (chair), Marco Ruiz, Priya Nair, Ethan Brooks, Lina Chen
Attendees: eng-release-engineering, infra-oncall, platform-sre, solutions-eng rep

1) Quick timeline (UTC)
- 02:04: baseline deploy of serving-runtime@v2.1.3 with batching opt enabled (canary 0.5% traffic)
- 02:13: canary telemetry shows 4-6% 5xxs and p95 latency jump from 210ms -> 420ms
- 02:16: canary gateway auto-evicts canary traffic; rollout paused automatically
- 02:18: autoscaler attempted scale-up; several us-west1 nodes preempted, scale didn't reach expected capacity until 02:28
- 02:20: hotfix branch prepared (revert batching registry change) PR#3421 opened
- 02:34: hotfix promoted to canary; canary metrics returned to baseline by 02:42
- 03:00: progressive rollout resumed with adjusted canary rules; full rollout completed by 04:20

2) Observed impact and metrics
- Errors: spike concentrated on token-generation API (text-generation) only; embedding endpoints unaffected
- Error type: transient OOM-like failures in worker logs (OOM killed processes) + upstream 502s from gateway
- Latency: p95 doubled during spike window, p99 showed larger tail but low overall percent of requests
- Cost: autoscaler churn increased short-term instance spend; estimated additional cost ~$800 for surge window

3) Initial root cause hypothesis (triage)
- Primary: batching optimization change (commit 8f4b2c3) increased memory footprint per-inference on longer sequences; combined with a KV cache TTL mismatch caused cache thrash -> memory pressure -> OOMs on a subset of shards
- Secondary: autoscaler min-instances set to 0 for this pool and preemption events in us-west1 prevented quick replacement; scale-up loop backoff configured too aggressively
- Tertiary: canary acceptance criteria were too narrow (only error-rate threshold, not memory or resident-set-size signals)

4) Why hotfix worked
- Hotfix reverted the batching registry change; memory usage back to previous baseline so worker processes no longer hit OOM thresholds
- Canary rollback allowed safe verification before full rollout

5) Lessons learned / coaching notes (informal)
- Always include resident memory and RSS-based alarms in canary metrics for model-serving changes.
- Preflight: run real-world long-sequence synthetic workload as part of canary smoke checks (not just short token tests).
- Autoscaler config: set a conservative min-instances for critical gpu pools during deployments that touch runtime or batching.
- Document deploy-time risk flags in PR template: "changes memory footprint", "touches batching logic", "KV-cache changes"

6) Revised canary acceptance criteria (actionable)
- Error rate <= 0.5% over 5 minutes AND
- p95 latency within 1.5x baseline AND
- Average RSS per worker < 1.2x baseline AND
- No OOM/killed process events in worker logs for 10 minutes
- Canary must pass a synthetic long-sequence job (90th percentile sequence length representative of production)

7) Short-term mitigations (to implement immediately)
- Set min_instances=2 for serving-gpu-pool in us-west1 during next 72h deployment windows (Priya)
- Add RSS and OOM flags to canary monitor dashboard and to the deployment webhook (Marco)
- Add temporary guardrail to block merges that change batching config without SRE + ML review (Aisha & Lina)

8) Long-term fixes / roadmap items
- Rework batching registry to expose memory cost estimator per model config (research+applied-ml)
- Improve autoscaler backoff logic to consider preemption events and accelerate replacement (infra)
- KV-cache TTL audit and align default TTLs across runtime and cache-population components (platform-eng)
- Expand canary smoke suite to include multi-shard and long-sequence synthetic load tests (qa + eng-release-engineering)

9) Open questions (unresolved)
- Why did preemption cluster events align with this deploy? need infra logs correlation (INFRA-4321)
- Are there specific model family configs that systematically increase memory usage with the new batching opt? need regression tests from applied-ml

10) Action items (owner — due)
- Priya Nair — set min_instances=2 for serving-gpu-pool us-west1 for 72h (due 2025-01-23)
- Marco Ruiz — add RSS + OOM alerting to canary dashboard, create deployment webhook integration (due 2025-01-25)
- Aisha Patel & Lina Chen — add PR guardrail and update PR template to require SRE/ML review on batching/cache changes (due 2025-01-24)
- Ethan Brooks — run a KV-cache TTL audit and produce list of mismatched TTLs (due 2025-01-30)
- Applied-ML team (action ticket) — implement memory cost estimator prototype for batching registry (target Q1 milestone)

11) Notes to follow-up on during next standup
- Share capacity burn graphs for the surge window and updated autoscaler events
- Verify canary smoke test coverage includes long-sequence case and confirm test passing on next canary
- Confirm whether other regional pools had similar but suppressed incidents

Raw snippets / working thoughts (informal):
- "saw a cluster of OOMs concentrated on 3/16 shards — suspect batching pooling multiplied per-request memory allocation"
- "canary felt like it failed faster than we could evaporate traffic because the gateway returned 502s rather than 5xxs in some cases"
- "PR checklist update is low friction and will stop a class of regressions — do it"

Meeting closed: 2025-01-22 03:45 UTC
Prepared by: Aisha Patel
Reviewers: Marco Ruiz, Priya Nair, Lina Chen
